evidence.explanation: Records hypergammaglobulinemia as a common laboratory consequence, without an established mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Growth hormone insensitivity (GHI) syndrome, first described in 1966, is classically associated with monogenic defects in the GH receptor (GHR) gene which result in severe post-natal growth failure as consequences of insulin-like growth factor I (IGF-I) deficiency.
evidence.explanation: Establishes GHR as the classic causative gene for GHIS.

evidence.snippet: The critical importance of STAT5B in human IGF-I production was confirmed with the identification of the first homozygous, autosomal recessive, STAT5B mutation in a young female patient who phenotypically resembled patients with classical growth hormone insensitivity (GHI) syndrome (Laron syndrome) due to mutations in the GHR gene, presenting with severe postnatal growth failure and marked IGF-I deficiency.
evidence.explanation: Establishes homozygous, autosomal recessive STAT5B loss of function as a cause of GH insensitivity.

genes/1.notes: Split from the dominant-negative heterozygous record below because the two are separate MONDO concepts (MONDO:0100211 and MONDO:0100219) with different inheritance and different immunologic risk, and because `subtype:` is single-valued. Detailed immunologic curation of this arm lives in kb/disorders/STAT5B_Deficiency.yaml.

evidence.snippet: We now report the first germline heterozygous STAT5B variants with dominant-negative effects, identified by targeted and whole-exome sequencing (WES), in short-statured subjects from three unrelated families.
evidence.explanation: Documents dominant-negative STAT5B variants as a cause of GHIS, in addition to the recessive form.

evidence.snippet: Biallelic IGFALS variants lead to acid‒labile subunit (ALS) deficiency characterized by growth hormone resistance with or without delayed puberty.
evidence.explanation: Establishes biallelic (loss-of-function) IGFALS variants as causative of ALS deficiency, a GH-resistance subtype of GHIS.

evidence.snippet: He showed short stature consistent with ALS deficiency.
evidence.explanation: Documents a patient with biallelic IGFALS variants and short stature (ALS deficiency).

evidence.snippet: the recent identification of human IGF1 and IGF1 receptor (IGF1R) mutations, as well as information obtained from transgenic animals, points to a strong genetic component being of pivotal importance in the development of growth retardation.
evidence.explanation: Establishes IGF1R mutations as a genetic cause of growth retardation (IGF-1 resistance).

evidence.snippet: The importance of IGF-I for both in utero as well as postnatal human growth is highlighted by rare human homozygous IGF1 mutations, which are characterized by intrauterine growth retardation (IUGR), microcephaly, mental retardation and severe postnatal growth failure.
evidence.explanation: Establishes homozygous IGF1 loss-of-function variants as a cause of intrauterine and postnatal growth failure within the GH-IGF-I axis.

genes/5.notes: Recorded here so the IGF1 arm of this umbrella is a declared causal gene and not only a gene descriptor on the IGF1 Deficiency subtype row. Detailed curation of the disease itself is in kb/disorders/IGF1_Deficiency.yaml (MONDO:0012110) and is not duplicated.

evidence.snippet: treatment in children and adolescents with severe growth failure due to severe primary IGF-I deficiency (SPIGFD)
evidence.explanation: Real-world registry establishes rhIGF-1 (mecasermin) as the treatment for severe primary IGF-I deficiency, the regulatory category covering GHIS subtypes.

evidence.snippet: During the first 6 months of treatment, height velocity increased to 7.8 and 8.4 cm/year without any clinical evidence of side-effects.
evidence.explanation: Early trial demonstrating the growth-promoting efficacy of rhIGF-1 in Laron syndrome.

treatments/0.description: Recombinant human IGF-1 (rhIGF-1; mecasermin, Increlex) is the mainstay disease-specific therapy for the IGF-1-deficiency subtypes of GHIS (GHR, STAT5B, IGF1, IGFALS). By directly supplying IGF-1 it bypasses the receptor/ signaling block; GH itself is ineffective because the defect is GH resistance. The IGF1R-resistance subtype responds poorly because the defect is the receptor. Dose with meals - hypoglycemia is the principal adverse effect.

evidence.snippet: During the first 6 months of treatment, height velocity increased to 7.8 and 8.4 cm/year without any clinical evidence of side-effects.
evidence.explanation: rhIGF-1 restores growth-plate signaling and increases height velocity in Laron syndrome, bypassing the receptor defect.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Mecasermin supplies exogenous IGF-1, bypassing the upstream GH-receptor/ signaling block to restore IGF-1 action.

evidence.snippet: Growth hormone insensitivity (GHI) syndrome, first described in 1966, is classically associated with monogenic defects in the GH receptor (GHR) gene which result in severe post-natal growth failure as consequences of insulin-like growth factor I (IGF-I) deficiency.
evidence.explanation: Indirect/mechanistic evidence: because GHIS is GH insensitivity at or below the receptor, GH therapy is not expected to correct the downstream IGF-1 deficiency. The snippet establishes the mechanism rather than directly experimentally refuting GH therapy.

treatments/1.description: Recombinant human GH is ineffective in the primary GHIS subtypes because the lesion is at or downstream of the GH receptor; failure of IGF-1 to rise on GH stimulation is in fact the diagnostic confirmatory test.

evidence.snippet: Mutations identified have been predominantly recessive.
evidence.explanation: Predominantly recessive inheritance underpins the value of genetic counseling for at-risk families.

treatments/2.description: Genetic counseling addresses the (predominantly) autosomal recessive recurrence risk and is especially relevant in the consanguineous/founder populations where GHR and other axis defects cluster.

evidence.snippet: Human mutations in STAT5A, as noted above, have yet to be identified.
evidence.explanation: Confirms that human disease-causing STAT5A variants were not established, defining the knowledge gap.

open_questions/0.rationale: STAT5A shares >95% identity with STAT5B and is activated by the same GHR-JAK2 cascade, yet the two paralogs are non-redundant. STAT5A is therefore a mechanistically plausible post-receptor GHIS node, but as of the key reviews human disease-causing STAT5A variants had not been reported, so the STAT5A subtype is included as a candidate pending human genetic confirmation. Targeted/exome sequencing of STAT5A in GHIS patients lacking GHR/STAT5B/IGFALS/IGF1/IGF1R variants, with functional testing of candidate variants for IGF1 transcriptional output, would resolve the gap.

evidence.snippet: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection has become an important etiological driver of oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), leading to unique tumor characteristics.
evidence.explanation: Identifies HPV infection as the etiological driver of oropharyngeal SCC.

steps/1.description: HPV E6 oncoprotein recruits the E3 ubiquitin ligase E6AP to target p53 for proteasomal degradation, eliminating DNA damage checkpoints and allowing survival of cells with genomic instability. Unlike HPV-negative HNSCC, TP53 mutations are rare in HPV-positive tumors.

steps/2.description: HPV E7 oncoprotein binds and degrades the retinoblastoma protein (pRB), releasing E2F transcription factors to drive S-phase entry. This causes compensatory overexpression of p16INK4a, which serves as a clinical biomarker for HPV-associated tumors.

steps/3.description: HPV genome integration into the host chromosome disrupts the E2 viral repressor, leading to constitutive E6/E7 expression. However, episomal HPV may also drive carcinogenesis in some HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancers.

steps/4.description: HPV-positive HNSCC evades immune surveillance through downregulation of antigen presentation and PD-L1 expression. However, these tumors are generally more immunogenic than HPV-negative HNSCC, contributing to better prognosis and response to immunotherapy.

evidence.snippet: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection has become an important etiological driver of oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), leading to unique tumor characteristics.
evidence.explanation: Supports treating HPV infection as the initiating exposure acting on the E6-mediated mechanism curated here.

edges/0.description: Infection of the oropharyngeal epithelium is what introduces the E6 oncoprotein, so the exposure initiates the earliest curated mechanism.

genes/0.notes: Unlike HPV-negative HNSCC where TP53 mutations occur in greater than 80% of cases, HPV-positive tumors typically have wild-type TP53 because p53 function is eliminated through E6-mediated degradation.

genes/1.notes: PIK3CA mutations occur in approximately 20-30% of HPV-positive HNSCC, activating PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling. This is the most commonly mutated oncogene in HPV-positive tumors.

genes/2.notes: CDKN2A (p16) is typically wild-type and overexpressed in HPV-positive HNSCC due to E7-mediated pRB inactivation, in contrast to HPV-negative HNSCC where CDKN2A is frequently deleted or silenced.

treatments/0.description: Concurrent cisplatin-based chemotherapy with intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) is standard treatment for most HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancers. The excellent prognosis has led to de-escalation trials aiming to reduce long-term treatment toxicity.

treatments/1.description: Minimally invasive transoral robotic surgery (TORS) allows resection of oropharyngeal tumors with reduced morbidity compared to traditional open surgery. May be followed by adjuvant radiation based on pathologic features.

treatments/2.description: PD-1 inhibitors (pembrolizumab, nivolumab) are approved for recurrent or metastatic HNSCC. HPV-positive tumors may have enhanced immunogenicity due to viral antigen expression, though clinical response rates are similar to HPV-negative disease.

treatments/3.description: Prophylactic HPV vaccination is expected to reduce the incidence of HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer, though the impact will not be fully realized for several decades due to the long latency between infection and cancer development.

evidence.snippet: Twenty-five cases of HSTCL were identified. Twenty-two (88%) patients had inflammatory bowel disease and three had rheumatoid arthritis.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the immunosuppressed inflammatory-disease population in which these cases arose.

evidence.snippet: HSTCL is no longer restricted to the previously identified risk group of young male patients, but can also occur in patients with rheumatoid arthritis, females and older adults receiving TNF-α inhibitors and immunomodulators.
evidence.explanation: Qualifies the classic young-male IBD stereotype, which is why this entry does not state the association as a demographic rule.

evidence.snippet: None of the 12 HSTCL patients had been treated with an anti-tumor necrosis factor-α agent.
evidence.explanation: Supports this entry's claim that the exposure is neither necessary nor confined to the classic group: a complete-capture national series accrued twelve cases with no anti-TNF exposure at all. Graded INDIRECT because non-necessity follows by inference from the absence rather than being asserted. It is SUPPORT, not REFUTE, because the claim being evidenced is the qualified one this entry makes, not the stronger reading that the exposure is required.

evidence.snippet: Cytogenetic abnormalities included isochromosome 7q (i7q) in 8 (62%) of 13 and trisomy 8 in 4 (44%) of 9.
evidence.explanation: Establishes isochromosome 7q as the dominant recurrent cytogenetic abnormality in a consecutive single-institution HSTCL cohort.

steps/3.description: Isochromosome 7q, with loss of 7p and gain of 7q material, is the characteristic cytogenetic lesion of HSTCL and is present in the majority of karyotyped cases, frequently alongside trisomy 8. It is treated here as the transforming somatic event in the gamma/delta T-cell compartment.

evidence.snippet: HSTLs manifest frequent mutations in STAT5B (31%), STAT3 (9%), and PIK3CD (9%), for which there currently exist potential targeted therapies.
evidence.explanation: Whole-exome sequencing of 68 cases quantifies STAT5B as the dominant JAK-STAT lesion.

evidence.snippet: Mutations in STAT3 or STAT5B lead to activation of the JAK/STAT pathway, and mutations involving SETD2, IN080 and ARID1 are involved in chromatin modification.
evidence.explanation: Review statement naming the pathway consequence of the STAT5B lesion.

steps/4.description: Activating mutations in STAT5B, and less often STAT3, drive ligand-independent JAK-STAT signalling. STAT5B is the most frequently mutated signalling gene in HSTCL and the pathway is a candidate therapeutic target.

evidence.snippet: Chromatin-modifying genes, including SETD2, INO80, and ARID1B, were commonly mutated in HSTL, affecting 62% of cases.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies chromatin-modifier loss as the most frequent lesion class.

evidence.snippet: We experimentally demonstrated that SETD2 acts as a tumor suppressor gene.
evidence.explanation: Functional demonstration that SETD2 loss is causal rather than incidental.

steps/5.description: Loss-of-function mutation of chromatin-modifying genes is the most common lesion class in HSTCL, affecting the majority of cases; SETD2, INO80 and ARID1B are the recurrently affected members. SETD2, the H3K36 trimethyltransferase, is bound here as the exemplar because it is the most frequently silenced single gene and the one shown experimentally to act as a tumor suppressor. The 62% figure below is the frequency of the lesion class, not of SETD2 alone.

evidence.snippet: Flow cytometry studies showed cells with an unusual T-cell phenotype expressing the gamma delta T-cell receptor and restricted expression of the V delta 1 but not the V delta 2 protein, indicating the clonal nature of the proliferation.
evidence.explanation: Documents the restricted V-delta-1 gamma/delta phenotype and its clonality.

evidence.snippet: TCR delta gene rearrangements were detected in six out of the eight cases
evidence.explanation: Molecular confirmation of clonal T-cell receptor delta rearrangement in a series.

steps/6.description: A monoclonal population of cytotoxic T cells, usually expressing the gamma/delta T-cell receptor with restricted V-delta-1 usage, expands. Clonality is demonstrable by T-cell receptor gamma and delta gene rearrangement.

evidence.snippet: Histologically, lymphoma cells infiltrated the cords of Billroth and often packed the sinuses.
evidence.explanation: Describes the splenic red pulp infiltration pattern directly.

evidence.snippet: Liver biopsy showed lymphoma cell infiltrations in the sinusoids, and three cases showed involvements of the portal tracts.
evidence.explanation: Documents the hepatic sinusoidal infiltration that names the disease.

evidence.snippet: Patients present with extranodal disease involving the spleen, liver and bone marrow; lymphadenopathy is usually absent.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the three-compartment extranodal distribution and the absence of nodal disease that distinguishes HSTCL from most lymphomas.

steps/7.description: Neoplastic cells occupy the splenic red pulp cords and sinuses and the hepatic sinusoids, and infiltrate the bone marrow, producing organomegaly and cytopenias without nodal disease. This sinusoidal tropism is the defining tissue-level feature of the entity.

evidence.snippet: All patients presented with fever, with some exhibiting emaciation and/or hemophagocytic syndrome.
evidence.explanation: Establishes fever as universal and hemophagocytic syndrome as a recognised subset presentation in a 40-case series.

steps/8.description: A systemic inflammatory state accompanies the disease, producing fever in essentially all patients and, in a subset, hemophagocytic syndrome. Hemophagocytic syndrome at onset marks a harder-to-treat course with higher mortality.

evidence.snippet: Clinical characteristics include massive splenomegaly in 16 patients (73%), hepatic involvement in 13 (59%), and chronic immunosuppressed state in 8 (36%).
evidence.explanation: Quantifies massive splenomegaly in a consecutive HSTCL cohort.

steps/9.description: Splenomegaly is near-universal and characteristically massive, reflecting diffuse red pulp infiltration.

evidence.snippet: Clinical characteristics include massive splenomegaly in 16 patients (73%), hepatic involvement in 13 (59%), and chronic immunosuppressed state in 8 (36%).
evidence.explanation: Graded INDIRECT and left without a frequency: the cohort reports hepatic *involvement* in 59%, and says "massive splenomegaly" when it means enlargement, so the 59% cannot be read as a frequency for hepatomegaly specifically.

steps/10.description: Hepatic involvement with enlargement, from sinusoidal infiltration.

evidence.snippet: Common laboratory findings included leukopenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia.
evidence.explanation: Names thrombocytopenia directly as a common finding in a 40-case series, rather than inferring it from an undifferentiated cytopenia claim.

evidence.snippet: Patients with HSTCL commonly present with B-symptoms and cytopenias, which may suggest a diagnosis of acute leukemia initially.
evidence.explanation: Supporting context. Graded INDIRECT because the review does not break the cytopenias down by lineage, so thrombocytopenia follows only by inference.

steps/11.description: Cytopenias are a presenting feature and may suggest acute leukemia before the diagnosis is made.

evidence.snippet: There were 7 cases of leukopenia at disease onset, as well as 8 cases of anemia (Hb < 120 g/L), and 5 cases of thrombocytopenia (PLT < 100 × 109/L).
evidence.explanation: Cohort figure with an explicit haemoglobin threshold, replacing the single case report this claim previously rested on.

evidence.snippet: We describe a case of a middle-aged women who presented with anemia and mild hepatosplenomegaly
evidence.explanation: Retained as corroborating case-level detail, not as a frequency estimate.

steps/12.description: Anemia at presentation, from marrow infiltration and splenic sequestration.

evidence.snippet: Those patients suffering from hemophagocytic syndrome at the onset of this disease face greater treatment-related difficulties and a higher risk of mortality.
evidence.explanation: Documents hemophagocytic syndrome as an outcome-relevant feature of the disease.

steps/13.description: Hemophagocytic syndrome occurs in a subset of patients and is an adverse prognostic marker.

evidence.snippet: All patients presented with fever, with some exhibiting emaciation and/or hemophagocytic syndrome.
evidence.explanation: Fever was present in every patient in this 40-case series, which states the phenotype directly rather than inferring it from a B-symptoms claim.

steps/14.description: B symptoms, including fever, are a common presenting complex.

edges/2.description: The cytogenetic lesion establishes the clone from which the disease grows.

evidence.snippet: we found that mutations in STAT5B and PIK3CD activate critical signaling pathways important to cell survival in HSTL
evidence.explanation: Cites the experimental result linking the STAT5B lesion specifically to survival signalling in HSTCL cells, which is the causal step this edge asserts.

edges/3.description: Constitutive JAK-STAT signalling supports survival and proliferation of the neoplastic clone.

edges/4.description: Loss of the tumor suppressor removes a brake on proliferation of the clone.

edges/5.description: The expanded clone homes to and fills the sinusoidal compartments.

edges/6.description: The neoplastic clone drives a systemic inflammatory state, which in a subset of patients reaches frank hemophagocytic syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Twenty-four cases (96%) also received an immunomodulator (azathioprine, 6-mercaptopurine, or methotrexate).
evidence.explanation: In the FDA adverse-event series nearly every anti-TNF-associated case had concomitant immunomodulator exposure, which is the combination this link describes.

edges/13.description: Sustained pharmacologic immunosuppression is the setting in which the gamma/delta clone emerges in this subset of patients.

evidence.snippet: HSTLs manifest frequent mutations in STAT5B (31%), STAT3 (9%), and PIK3CD (9%), for which there currently exist potential targeted therapies.
evidence.explanation: Frequency of the STAT5B lesion across 68 exomes.

genes/0.notes: Activating mutations in STAT5B are the most frequent signalling lesion in HSTCL, found in roughly a third of sequenced cases.

evidence.snippet: We experimentally demonstrated that SETD2 acts as a tumor suppressor gene.
evidence.explanation: Functional evidence for the tumor-suppressor role.

genes/1.notes: SETD2 is the most frequently silenced gene in HSTCL and functions as a tumor suppressor in this disease.

evidence.snippet: Most HSTL patients are treated with combination chemotherapy and, when feasible, bone marrow transplantation, but relapses are frequent and the overwhelming majority of patients succumb to HSTL.
evidence.explanation: States the standard of care and, in the same sentence, its limits.

treatments/0.description: Combination chemotherapy is the backbone of initial treatment for most patients, with transplant added where feasible. Relapse is frequent and most patients die of the disease.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Cytotoxic therapy directed at the proliferating neoplastic clone.

evidence.snippet: Patients who underwent splenectomy followed by chemotherapy had a higher median and average survival time compared to those who only received chemotherapy.
evidence.explanation: Direct comparison of splenectomy-plus-chemotherapy against chemotherapy alone.

treatments/1.description: Splenectomy followed by chemotherapy was associated with longer survival than chemotherapy alone in a 40-case series, and three of the four long-term survivors in a separate institutional cohort had splenectomy as part of initial treatment.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: Removes the dominant compartment of tumor burden and the site of splenic sequestration driving the cytopenias.

evidence.snippet: although several studies support a role for allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant
evidence.explanation: Review position on the role of allogeneic transplant.

evidence.snippet: our data do not show a statistically significant benefit of splenectomy and/or allo-HCT, likely as a result of our small sample size.
evidence.explanation: Recorded as REFUTE so the negative result stays visible, and INDIRECT because it bears on the claim only through inference: the tested exposure is the composite "splenectomy and/or allo-HCT" rather than transplant alone, and the authors read their own null as underpowered rather than as absence of benefit.

treatments/2.description: There is no consensus standard of care. Several studies support a role for allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant, though the largest single-centre series did not demonstrate a statistically significant benefit, which it attributed to sample size.

evidence.snippet: Moreover, 3 of 4 long-term survivors had splenectomy as part of initial treatment, and 2 of 4 long-term survivors received an allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant (allo-HCT).
evidence.explanation: Half of the long-term survivors in this cohort received allogeneic transplant. Graded INDIRECT because survival after transplant is an outcome from which clearance of the neoplastic clone is inferred; the cohort does not measure clone eradication directly.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: Replaces the haematopoietic compartment harbouring the neoplastic clone.

evidence.snippet: A point mutation in exon 13 of the beta cardiac myosin heavy chain (MHC) gene is present in all individuals affected with familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (FHC) from a large kindred. This missense mutation converts a highly conserved arginine residue (Arg-403) to a glutamine.
evidence.explanation: The founding CMH1 report: co-segregation of the MYH7 R403Q missense variant with familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in a large kindred, establishing the beta-cardiac myosin heavy chain gene as a cause of the disease.

evidence.snippet: HCM is caused by mutations in the genes encoding the fundamental force-generating machinery of the cardiac muscle, including β-cardiac myosin.
evidence.explanation: Places the MYH7 lesion in the force-generating machinery of the sarcomere, the trigger for this entity.

steps/1.description: The initiating lesion in CMH1 is a heterozygous missense variant in MYH7, the gene encoding the beta-cardiac myosin heavy chain — the ATP-hydrolysing motor of the sarcomeric thick filament. The founding example, and still the archetype, is Arg403Gln (R403Q), the first mutation ever linked to familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; R403Q sits in the globular myosin head (S1), the region responsible for actin interaction and motor function. In contrast to the truncating, haploinsufficiency mechanism of MYBPC3 disease, most MYH7 alleles are missense changes that are stably expressed and incorporated into the sarcomere as a mutant motor, so the mutant protein perturbs contraction directly rather than by its absence.

evidence.snippet: folded-back sequestered state referred to as the interacting heads motif (IHM) lead to a significant increase in the number of heads functionally accessible for interaction with actin.
evidence.explanation: Direct biochemical evidence that MYH7 HCM mutations at IHM interfaces release sequestered heads, increasing the number available to interact with actin.

evidence.snippet: The G256E mutation disrupts the transducer region of the S1 head and reduces the fraction of myosin in the folded-back state by 33%, resulting in more myosin heads available for contraction.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the size of the SRX shift for a named MYH7 allele, and shows the destabilizing lesion need not sit on an IHM contact surface itself — G256E acts through the transducer region of the motor domain.

evidence.snippet: hypercontractility is due to an increase in the number of myosin heads (S1) that are accessible for force production.
evidence.explanation: States the core hypothesis this node captures: HCM hypercontractility arises from an increase in the number of force-producing heads freed from the sequestered state.

evidence.snippet: destabilized the super relaxed state in longer, two-headed myosin constructs, freeing more heads to generate force.
evidence.explanation: Shows a specific MYH7 mutation (P710R) destabilizing the super-relaxed state and freeing heads for force generation.

evidence.snippet: Some mutations which cause hypertrophic or dilated cardiomyopathies alter the SRX-DRX equilibrium, but not all mutations.
evidence.explanation: Important caveat curated with the node: SRX-DRX destabilization is a common but not universal consequence of cardiomyopathy myosin mutations, so this arm applies to the large subset of alleles that shift the equilibrium rather than to every MYH7 variant, so the support it gives this node is indirect.

steps/2.description: In the resting sarcomere a large fraction of myosin heads occupy the super-relaxed (SRX) state — folded back against the thick-filament backbone in the interacting-heads motif (IHM), with very low ATPase activity, forming an energy-conserving reserve of motors withheld from force generation. Many MYH7 HCM mutations map to the interfaces that stabilize this folded-back state (the myosin mesa, the head-head and head-tail contacts), and they weaken those intramolecular interactions. The result is release of sequestered heads from the SRX/IHM into the disordered-relaxed state, so more heads become functionally accessible to actin — the molecular origin of hypercontractility shared across a large subset of MYH7 alleles.

evidence.snippet: The major change in the R453C human β-cardiac subfragment 1 is a 50% increase in the intrinsic force of the motor compared with wild type, with no appreciable change in the stroke size, as observed with a dual-beam optical trap.
evidence.explanation: Single-molecule optical-trap measurement of a raised intrinsic force for an MYH7 mutant motor, predicting a hypercontractile ensemble.

evidence.snippet: Overall, this study suggests that the R453C mutation should result in a hypercontractile state in the heart muscle.
evidence.explanation: States the functional conclusion — a hypercontractile state — that the motor-level force change produces.

evidence.snippet: This correlation suggests that faster cross-bridge relaxation kinetics results in an increase in energetic cost of tension generation in human HCM with the R403Q mutation compared to HCMsmn.
evidence.explanation: Direct measurement in human R403Q myocardium (single myofibrils and muscle strips) linking faster cross-bridge kinetics to an increased energetic cost of tension generation, evidence obtained in patient cardiac tissue.

steps/3.description: Beyond releasing sequestered heads, individual MYH7 missense alleles alter the mechanochemistry of the motor stroke itself. Single-molecule and myofibril studies show mutation-specific changes — increased intrinsic force per cross-bridge, and faster cross-bridge detachment kinetics — that together raise the force generated by the ensemble of motors and increase the ATP consumed per unit tension (tension cost). The energetic penalty, measured directly in human myocardium carrying R403Q, is a distinctive feature of the beta-myosin motor lesion and links the molecular defect to the myocardial energy deficit seen in HCM.

evidence.snippet: produced significantly increased force (measured by traction force microscopy) compared with isogenic control cells.
evidence.explanation: Isogenic human iPSC-cardiomyocyte evidence that an MYH7 HCM mutation increases cellular contractile force.

evidence.snippet: Cardiac muscle hypercontractility is a key pathophysiological abnormality in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and a major determinant of dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction.
evidence.explanation: Confirms hypercontractility as the central pathophysiological abnormality of HCM and links it to outflow obstruction. Directness is INDIRECT because the trial enrolled obstructive HCM broadly rather than genotyped MYH7 carriers, so the claim about this entity follows by an inference step.

steps/4.description: At the cell level the molecular changes converge on hypercontractility: CRISPR-edited human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes carrying an MYH7 HCM mutation generate significantly greater contractile force than isogenic controls. Because the same lesion disturbs cross-bridge relaxation kinetics, systolic hypercontraction is accompanied by impaired diastolic relaxation. This hypercontractile, poorly relaxing cell state — a key pathophysiological abnormality of HCM and the determinant of dynamic outflow obstruction — is the cellular phenotype the cardiac myosin inhibitors were designed to normalize.

evidence.snippet: Using engineered cardiac microtissues (CMTs) composed of HCM-causing MYH7-variant hiPSC-CMs and wild-type fibroblasts, we observed cell-cell cross-talk leading to increased collagen deposition, tissue stiffening, and decreased contractility dependent on fibroblast proliferation.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the node: MYH7-variant cardiomyocytes activate neighbouring fibroblasts, and the resulting collagen deposition and stiffening depend on fibroblast proliferation.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, inhibiting epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase with erlotinib hydrochloride attenuated stromal activation.
evidence.explanation: Identifies EGFR as the transducing receptor by pharmacological loss of function, which is what makes this a named signalling arm rather than an unspecified paracrine effect.

evidence.snippet: R403Q+/- CMTs exhibited a 40% increase in collagen I content compared to WT CMTs
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the matrix effect against an isogenic wild-type control in the archetypal CMH1 allele.

steps/5.description: Interstitial fibrosis in CMH1 is not solely a passive response to wall stress. In engineered cardiac microtissues built from MYH7 R403Q hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes co-cultured with wild-type ventricular cardiac fibroblasts, the mutant cardiomyocytes release paracrine factors that drive fibroblast proliferation and collagen deposition. Collagen I content rose 40% over isogenic wild-type microtissues and the tissue stiffened, and the effect depended on fibroblast proliferation rather than on cardiomyocyte matrix output. Epidermal growth factor alone was sufficient to stimulate the stromal cells, and inhibiting EGFR tyrosine kinase with erlotinib attenuated the activation — identifying EGFR signalling as the transducing arm and, in principle, a druggable one. The same microtissue system shows that the tissue-level consequence is hypocontractility even while the individual mutant cardiomyocytes are hypercontractile, which is how a cell-autonomous gain of contractile function ends up producing a stiff, poorly contracting ventricle.

evidence.snippet: substantial contractile variability from cardiomyocyte to cardiomyocyte within a patient's myocardium, much higher than in controls.
evidence.explanation: Documents the cell-to-cell contractile variability in beta-MyHC-mutant patient myocardium that this node captures.

evidence.snippet: contractile imbalance due to unequal fractions of mutated and wildtype protein among individual cardiomyocytes over time will induce cardiomyocyte disarray and fibrosis, hallmarks of HCM.
evidence.explanation: States the contractile-imbalance hypothesis linking unequal mutant-allele expression to disarray and fibrosis, the hallmarks of HCM.

steps/6.description: A mechanism specific to the missense/poison-peptide biology of MYH7 disease. Because the mutant and wild-type MYH7 alleles are transcribed in a random, burst-like fashion and independently of one another, the fraction of mutant beta-myosin varies markedly from cardiomyocyte to cardiomyocyte within a single patient's myocardium. This produces much greater cell-to-cell variability of contractile function than in control hearts. The resulting mechanical mismatch between adjacent, differently loaded myocytes is proposed to drive the myofiber disarray and interstitial fibrosis that are hallmarks of HCM, providing a route from the molecular lesion to the tissue phenotype that does not depend on the average level of hypercontractility alone.

evidence.snippet: The histological features of HCM include myocyte hypertrophy and disarray, as well as interstitial fibrosis.
evidence.explanation: Names the defining tissue-level triad — myocyte hypertrophy, disarray, and interstitial fibrosis — that this node represents.

evidence.snippet: Cellular hypertrophy was prevented in the P710R cells by inhibition of ERK or Akt.
evidence.explanation: Implicates ERK and Akt growth signalling downstream of the MYH7 mechanical lesion in producing the cellular hypertrophy of this node.

evidence.snippet: contractile imbalance due to unequal fractions of mutated and wildtype protein among individual cardiomyocytes over time will induce cardiomyocyte disarray and fibrosis, hallmarks of HCM.
evidence.explanation: Ties the upstream contractile imbalance to the disarray and fibrosis of this tissue node.

steps/7.description: Chronic hypercontractility with raised energetic cost, amplified by cell-to-cell contractile imbalance, drives the structural remodeling that defines the clinical phenotype: cardiomyocyte hypertrophy — typically asymmetric and septal-predominant — together with myofiber disarray and interstitial and replacement fibrosis. Pro-hypertrophic growth signalling contributes: in an MYH7-mutant human iPSC-cardiomyocyte model, cellular hypertrophy was prevented by inhibition of ERK or Akt, implicating those pathways downstream of the mechanical stimulus. Fibrosis provides the substrate for both diastolic dysfunction and re-entrant arrhythmia.

evidence.snippet: There were no differences when the two most frequently affected genes, MYBPC3 and MYH7, were compared.
evidence.explanation: Records the important nuance that, at the cohort level, MYH7 and MYBPC3 do not differ significantly across the pooled clinical features, so MYH7 is not simply a uniformly more severe genotype than MYBPC3; it is one of the two commonest sarcomeric causes.

evidence.snippet: In the five families with HCM carrying MYH7-R453C mutations, genotype is highly correlated with clinical phenotype, and patients have a high risk of sudden death and poor prognosis.
evidence.explanation: A family study of a specific MYH7 variant documenting high sudden-death risk and poor prognosis, the arrhythmic endpoint of this node.

steps/8.description: The hypertrophied, disarrayed and fibrotic ventricle produces the clinical endpoints of CMH1. Hypercontractility with septal hypertrophy generates dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in a subset of patients; the stiff, poorly relaxing ventricle causes diastolic dysfunction; and the fibrotic, electrically heterogeneous substrate carries a risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmia and sudden cardiac death that is clinically important for MYH7 variants. Sarcomere-positive disease, of which MYH7 is a leading cause, presents younger and with a stronger family history of sudden death than sarcomere-negative HCM.

evidence.snippet: Cardiac muscle hypercontractility is a key pathophysiological abnormality in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and a major determinant of dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction.
evidence.explanation: Links hypercontractility to dynamic LVOT obstruction. Directness is INDIRECT because the trial population is obstructive HCM broadly rather than genotyped MYH7 carriers.

steps/9.description: Dynamic obstruction of the left ventricular outflow tract arises from hypercontractility combined with septal hypertrophy and systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve, defining the obstructive phenotype targeted by myosin inhibitors and septal reduction therapy.

evidence.snippet: Cross-bridge slow relaxation kinetics in single R403Q myofibrils was significantly higher (P < 0.0001) than in HCMsmn myofibrils
evidence.explanation: Documents disturbed cross-bridge relaxation kinetics in human R403Q myocardium, the molecular basis of the impaired relaxation underlying diastolic dysfunction.

steps/10.description: Impaired relaxation and increased chamber stiffness produce diastolic dysfunction, an early and characteristic functional consequence of the hypercontractile, poorly relaxing myocardium.

evidence.snippet: 2 experienced (F1Ⅲ1, F3Ⅲ3) events of sudden cardiac death survival
evidence.explanation: Aborted sudden cardiac death (survived cardiac arrest) in MYH7-R453C carriers evidences the malignant ventricular arrhythmia of this node.

steps/11.description: The electrically heterogeneous, fibrotic myocardium supports malignant ventricular arrhythmia, the proximate cause of sudden cardiac death in this disease.

evidence.snippet: 2(F1Ⅱ2, F3Ⅱ1) died from heart failure during the follow-up period.
evidence.explanation: Deaths from heart failure among MYH7-R453C carriers evidence heart failure as a clinical endpoint of the disease.

steps/12.description: Progressive diastolic dysfunction, and in a minority progression toward systolic impairment or an end-stage phase, produces heart failure symptoms.

evidence.snippet: Atrial fibrillation is also a common complication and is not well tolerated.
evidence.explanation: Establishes atrial fibrillation as a common and clinically consequential complication of the disease.

steps/13.description: Atrial fibrillation is a common complication of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, arising from the left atrial enlargement that follows chronically raised filling pressures. It is poorly tolerated because a hypertrophied, non-compliant ventricle depends on atrial contribution to filling, and it carries a substantial thromboembolic risk.

evidence.snippet: Nonsustained ventricular tachycardia, syncope, a family history of sudden cardiac death, and severe cardiac hypertrophy are major risk factors for sudden cardiac death.
evidence.explanation: Names syncope among the major sudden-death risk markers. Directness is INDIRECT on two counts: the source is a broad-HCM review rather than a MYH7 cohort, and the sentence establishes syncope as a risk marker, from which its occurrence as a clinical feature follows by inference rather than being stated.

steps/14.description: Unexplained syncope in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy may reflect dynamic outflow obstruction, an arrhythmic event, or an abnormal vascular response to exertion. It is one of the major risk markers used in sudden-death risk stratification, which is why it is curated as a phenotype in its own right rather than folded into the arrhythmia node.

evidence.snippet: The histological features of HCM include myocyte hypertrophy and disarray, as well as interstitial fibrosis.
evidence.explanation: Establishes interstitial fibrosis as a histological feature of the disease. Directness is INDIRECT because the source is a broad-HCM review.

evidence.snippet: In patients with HCM, LGE on c-MRI is a strong predictor of arrhythmic outcomes including SCD, aborted SCD, and appropriate ICD therapy.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the imaged fibrosis burden predicts arrhythmic outcome across 8 prospective studies and 3808 patients. Directness is INDIRECT because the pooled cohorts are broad HCM rather than genotyped MYH7 carriers.

steps/15.description: Interstitial and replacement fibrosis is a defining tissue-level feature of the disease and, when imaged as late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac magnetic resonance, is a measurable predictor of arrhythmic outcome rather than merely a structural description. It is the tissue substrate that links the mechanism modeled in this entry's pathophysiology to the arrhythmic risk modeled in its phenotypes.

edges/1.description: The mutant motor, incorporated into the thick filament, destabilizes the folded-back autoinhibited state that normally sequesters myosin heads.

edges/2.description: Heads released from the super-relaxed reserve, together with allele-specific changes in the motor stroke, raise ensemble force and the ATP cost of contraction.

edges/3.description: Raised ensemble force and disturbed cross-bridge kinetics translate into cellular hypercontractility with impaired diastolic relaxation.

edges/4.description: Because mutant and wild-type MYH7 alleles are transcribed in variable proportions between neighboring myocytes, hypercontractility is unevenly distributed across the myocardium.

evidence.snippet: hiPSC-CM conditioned media and single-nucleus RNA sequencing data suggested that fibroblast proliferation is mediated by paracrine signals from MYH7-variant cardiomyocytes.
evidence.explanation: Supports this specific edge rather than either node alone: conditioned medium transfers the effect, so the signal travels from the MYH7-variant cardiomyocyte to the fibroblast.

edges/5.description: The mutant cardiomyocyte does not remodel the interstitium by mechanical load alone: it secretes soluble factors that act on the neighbouring fibroblast population. What couples the contractile state to that secretion is not established. The source proposes a broader stress response, with mechanical signalling from the intrinsic hypercontractility as one candidate, and states that further work is needed to identify the ligands and receptors involved — so the edge is curated with unknown intermediates rather than as a direct link.

edges/6.description: Sustained hypercontractility with raised energetic cost drives the structural remodeling of the ventricle.

edges/7.description: Fibroblast activation and excess collagen deposition are the cellular mechanism of the interstitial fibrosis component of the tissue-level remodeling node.

edges/8.description: The same collagen deposition presenting as the clinically measurable fibrosis burden, imaged as late gadolinium enhancement.

edges/9.description: Mechanical mismatch between neighboring myocytes promotes disarray and fibrotic remodeling.

edges/11.description: The impaired-relaxation and reduced-compliance component of this node presenting as the measured clinical phenotype.

edges/12.description: The obstruction component of this node presenting as the clinical phenotype targeted by myosin inhibitors and septal reduction.

edges/13.description: Sustained diastolic dysfunction, and in a minority progression to systolic impairment, produce clinical heart failure.

edges/14.description: The arrhythmic component of this node presenting clinically. Curated with unknown intermediates because which of hypertrophy, disarray, fibrosis and ischaemia carries the arrhythmic substrate in any given patient is not resolved.

edges/15.description: Raised filling pressures enlarge the left atrium, and left atrial dimension is the intermediate that predicts atrial fibrillation in this disease.

edges/16.description: Syncope may arise from the outflow obstruction, from an arrhythmic event, or from an abnormal vascular response to exertion; which applies in a given episode is usually not determined.

evidence.snippet: MYH7 | HGNC:7577 | hypertrophic cardiomyopathy | MONDO:0005045 | AD | Definitive
evidence.explanation: ClinGen's Gene Curation Expert Panel classifies this gene-disease relationship as Definitive, which is the authority for curating the gene as CAUSATIVE rather than a candidate.

evidence.snippet: The presence of any sarcomere gene mutation was associated with a younger age at presentation (38.4 vs 46.0 years, p<0.0005), a family history of HCM (50.6% vs 23.1%, p<0.0005), a family history of SCD (27.0% vs 14.9%, p<0.0005) and greater MLVWT (21.0 vs 19.3 mm, p=0.03).
evidence.explanation: The cohort is sarcomere-mutation carriers across genes rather than MYH7 carriers, so this is class-level evidence that a sarcomere genotype shifts age at presentation and family history, and reaches MYH7 by an inference step; the same study's finding of no outcome difference between MYH7 and MYBPC3 carriers is recorded in this entry's pathophysiology.

evidence.snippet: Cardiac muscle hypercontractility is a key pathophysiological abnormality in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and a major determinant of dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction.
evidence.explanation: The pivotal phase 3 trial establishing the rationale and use of a cardiac myosin inhibitor targeting hypercontractility in obstructive HCM.

treatments/0.description: Mavacamten is a small-molecule allosteric inhibitor of cardiac myosin ATPase that reduces the number of force-generating actin-myosin cross-bridges, stabilizing myosin in the energy-sparing super-relaxed state. It directly counteracts the hypercontractility that is the central abnormality of HCM, and is approved for symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; because beta-cardiac myosin is the MYH7 gene product, the drug acts on the same motor that carries the CMH1 lesion.

evidence.snippet: cardiac myosin inhibitor mavacamten slows nucleotide release by an equal factor for both heavy meromyosin and subfragment 1, thus only indirectly influencing the occupancy time of the SRX state.
evidence.explanation: Establishes mavacamten's biochemical action on beta-cardiac myosin nucleotide handling and its effect on SRX-state occupancy, the node it targets.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Mavacamten stabilizes the super-relaxed state and reduces the number of heads available for force generation, directly opposing the SRX destabilization that drives hypercontractility.

evidence.snippet: Surgical myectomy performed to relieve outflow obstruction and severe symptoms in HCM was associated with long-term survival equivalent to that of the general population, and superior to obstructive HCM without operation.
evidence.explanation: The long-term survival result that establishes myectomy as more than symptomatic relief. Directness is INDIRECT because the cohort is obstructive HCM broadly rather than genotyped MYH7 carriers, and because the design is an observational comparison rather than a randomized one.

treatments/1.description: Surgical septal myectomy relieves severe drug-refractory left ventricular outflow tract obstruction by resecting hypertrophied basal septal muscle.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: Resecting hypertrophied basal septal muscle removes the anatomical substrate of the dynamic outflow gradient, acting on the obstruction component of this node.

evidence.snippet: In a high-risk HCM cohort, ICD interventions for life-threatening ventricular tachyarrhythmias were frequent and highly effective in restoring normal rhythm.
evidence.explanation: The multicenter registry result establishing device efficacy in high-risk HCM. Directness is INDIRECT because the 506-patient cohort is high-risk HCM broadly rather than genotyped MYH7 carriers.

evidence.snippet: ICD complications included inappropriate shocks in 136 patients (27%).
evidence.explanation: Recorded as REFUTE against an unqualified claim of net benefit: in the same registry that established efficacy, over a quarter of recipients received an inappropriate shock. Curated as a separate item with the opposite direction rather than hedged into the efficacy item, because the two sentences make opposite claims about the same intervention. Directness is INDIRECT for the same broad-HCM reason as its companion.

treatments/2.description: An implantable cardioverter-defibrillator provides secondary or primary prevention of sudden cardiac death in patients judged to be at high arrhythmic risk, terminating malignant ventricular arrhythmia.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: The device does not modify the arrhythmic substrate; it terminates the ventricular tachyarrhythmia that would otherwise cause death, so it acts on the outcome rather than on any upstream mechanism.

evidence.snippet: At 24 weeks, the mean change in the peak oxygen uptake was 1.8 ml per kilogram per minute (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.2 to 2.3) in the aficamten group and 0.0 ml per kilogram per minute (95% CI, -0.5 to 0.5) in the placebo group
evidence.explanation: The pivotal phase 3 efficacy result for this drug, against a placebo comparator. Directness is INDIRECT because SEQUOIA-HCM enrolled symptomatic obstructive HCM broadly rather than genotyped MYH7 carriers.

treatments/3.description: Aficamten is an oral selective cardiac myosin inhibitor. Like mavacamten it acts directly on the beta-cardiac myosin motor that carries the CMH1 lesion, reducing left ventricular outflow tract gradients by mitigating hypercontractility. In the phase 3 SEQUOIA-HCM trial it improved peak oxygen uptake in symptomatic obstructive disease.

evidence.snippet: Aficamten is an oral selective cardiac myosin inhibitor that reduces left ventricular outflow tract gradients by mitigating cardiac hypercontractility.
evidence.explanation: Supports this edge specifically: names hypercontractility as the mechanism the drug acts through, rather than merely reporting that the drug works.

treatments/3/targets/0.description: Myosin inhibition reduces the number of force-generating cross-bridges, opposing the hypercontractile cellular state at the point where the MYH7 lesion produces it.

evidence.snippet: Seventy-eight patients (66%) were maintained with disopyramide without the necessity for major non-pharmacologic intervention with surgical myectomy, alcohol ablation, or pacing; outflow gradient at rest decreased from 75 +/- 33 to 40 +/- 32 mm Hg (p < 0.0001)
evidence.explanation: Quantifies gradient reduction and the proportion managed medically. Directness is INDIRECT because the cohort is obstructive HCM broadly rather than genotyped MYH7 carriers.

evidence.snippet: Disopyramide therapy does not appear to be proarrhythmic in HCM and should be considered before proceeding to surgical myectomy or alternate strategies.
evidence.explanation: Records the safety finding that positions this drug ahead of septal reduction in the treatment sequence.

treatments/4.description: Disopyramide is a class Ia antiarrhythmic with strong negative inotropic action, used as add-on therapy to a beta-blocker for persistent left ventricular outflow tract obstruction. It reduces the subaortic gradient and can defer or avoid septal reduction therapy; its limits are vagolytic side effects and the need for QT monitoring.

evidence.snippet: Two-thirds of obstructed HCM patients treated with disopyramide could be managed medically with amelioration of symptoms and about 50% reduction in subaortic gradient over >/=3 years.
evidence.explanation: Names the subaortic gradient as the quantity the drug moves and gives the size of the effect, which is the content of this edge rather than of the treatment record as a whole. Directness is INDIRECT because the series is obstructive HCM broadly rather than genotyped MYH7 carriers.

treatments/4/targets/0.description: The negative inotropic effect reduces the dynamic subaortic gradient, acting on the obstruction component of this node rather than on the underlying sarcomeric lesion.

evidence.snippet: The Euro-ASA registry demonstrated low peri-procedural and long-term mortality after ASA. This intervention provided durable relief of symptoms and a reduction of LV outflow tract obstruction in selected and highly symptomatic patients with obstructive HCM.
evidence.explanation: The largest multinational ablation registry (1275 patients, median 5.7 years) establishing durability and peri-procedural safety. Directness is INDIRECT because the cohort is obstructive HCM broadly rather than genotyped MYH7 carriers.

treatments/5.description: Catheter-based infarction of the basal septum through a septal perforator branch, an alternative to surgical myectomy for drug-refractory obstruction in patients who are poor surgical candidates. It does not address concomitant mitral or subvalvular abnormalities, which is where myectomy is preferred.

evidence.snippet: Alcohol septal ablation reduced the LV outflow tract gradient from 67 ± 36 to 16 ± 21 mmHg (P < 0.01) and NYHA class from 2.9 ± 0.5 to 1.6 ± 0.7 (P < 0.01).
evidence.explanation: Supports this edge specifically: names the outflow gradient as the quantity the procedure moves and gives the size of the reduction across 1275 patients. Directness is INDIRECT because the registry is obstructive HCM broadly rather than genotyped MYH7 carriers.

treatments/5/targets/0.description: Reduces basal septal muscle mass, relieving the mechanical obstruction component of this node.

evidence.snippet: In this study we identify an adenine base editor and single-guide RNA system that can efficiently correct this human PV with minimal bystander editing and off-target editing at selected sites.
evidence.explanation: Establishes correction of the archetypal CMH1 allele, R403Q, as technically achievable with acceptable editing specificity.

evidence.snippet: In vivo application of hpCas13d to 2 hypertrophic cardiomyopathy models caused by distinct human MYH7 analogous sequence variations specifically suppressed the altered allele and prevented cardiac hypertrophy.
evidence.explanation: The alternative allele-directed strategy: silencing the mutant transcript rather than correcting the gene, which suits a dominant-negative missense mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Together, these data indicated that base editing of the mutant R403Q allele, delivered several months or only weeks in advance of the typical time for disease manifestations, resulted in durable prevention of ventricular remodeling and hypertrophy.
evidence.explanation: The independent contemporaneous demonstration that a single in vivo editing dose durably prevents the remodeling phenotype in an R403Q mouse, curated alongside the correction and silencing strategies above so the treatment record does not rest on a single group.

treatments/6.description: Two preclinical strategies target the MYH7 allele itself rather than its downstream consequences. Adenine base editing corrects the pathogenic base in patient-derived cardiomyocytes and in humanized mice; high-precision Cas13d instead degrades the mutant transcript while sparing the wild-type allele, which suits the dominant-negative biology of missense MYH7 disease. Neither is an approved therapy, and both face delivery, durability and off-target questions. They are curated here because they are the only interventions in this entry that act on the trigger node.

evidence.snippet: We show that delivery of base editing components rescues pathological manifestations of HCM in induced pluripotent stem cell cardiomyocytes derived from patients with HCM and in a humanized mouse model of HCM.
evidence.explanation: Supports the edge specifically: correcting the MYH7 base rescues the disease phenotype, which is what establishes the trigger node as the target being acted on.

treatments/6/targets/0.description: Base editing removes the causal substitution and RNA-targeting Cas13d suppresses the mutant transcript, so both act on the initiating lesion rather than on any downstream mechanism.

evidence.snippet: In patients with mild or moderately symptomatic hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, exercise capacity was not improved by nadolol or verapamil, and individuals were more often impaired by nadolol than with verapamil.
evidence.explanation: Recorded as REFUTE against the claim that beta-blockade improves functional capacity: in this randomized crossover trial it did not, and nadolol impaired peak work load more often than verapamil did. Directness is INDIRECT because the trial enrolled broad HCM rather than genotyped MYH7 carriers, and because it was restricted to mildly and moderately symptomatic patients.

evidence.snippet: Despite the effects on exercise capacity, 13 patients (81%) preferred drug treatment (8 verapamil, 5 nadolol) over placebo (p = 0.001).
evidence.explanation: The counterpart to the item above, and the reason both drugs remain in use: patients preferred active drug to placebo even where objective exercise capacity did not improve. Curated as a separate item because the sentence supports a different claim from the one the CONCLUSIONS sentence refutes.

treatments/7.description: A non-vasodilating beta-blocker is the conventional first-line drug for symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, reducing the dynamic outflow gradient through negative inotropy and chronotropy and lengthening diastolic filling time. The evidence base is weaker than its first-line position suggests: in the only randomized placebo-controlled crossover trial in mildly to moderately symptomatic patients, nadolol did not improve maximal oxygen consumption and reduced peak exercise work load in most patients, though a majority still preferred active drug to placebo.

treatments/7/targets/0.description: Negative inotropy reduces the dynamic subaortic gradient and slower heart rates lengthen diastolic filling, so the drug acts on the obstruction and filling components of this node rather than on the sarcomeric lesion.

evidence.snippet: Verapamil improved reported performance at work compared with nadolol (p = 0.01) and tended to improve other measures of health-related behavior and symptoms compared with nadolol and placebo.
evidence.explanation: The head-to-head result placing verapamil ahead of a beta-blocker on patient-reported measures, which is why it is curated as a distinct treatment rather than a footnote to beta-blockade. Directness is INDIRECT because the trial enrolled broad HCM rather than genotyped MYH7 carriers.

treatments/8.description: A non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker used when beta-blockade is ineffective or not tolerated. It improves diastolic filling and reduces symptoms, and in direct comparison was better tolerated than nadolol. Guidelines caution against it in severe outflow obstruction with hypotension because its vasodilator effect can worsen the gradient.

treatments/8/targets/0.description: Acts on the diastolic-filling component of this node; unlike the myosin inhibitors it does not target the contractile lesion itself.

evidence.snippet: AF is common in HCM and associated with high thromboembolic risk. LA dimension and age are independently associated with AF but the literature is insufficient to create robust clinical tools to predict AF or thromboembolism. Most data suggest that AF patients should be anticoagulated.
evidence.explanation: The pooled basis for anticoagulating on the arrhythmia alone, and an explicit statement that the evidence does not support a prediction tool. Directness is INDIRECT because the 7381-patient pooled population is broad HCM rather than genotyped MYH7 carriers.

evidence.snippet: A population of 7381 patients (33 studies) revealed overall AF prevalence of 22.45% (95% CI 20.13% to 24.77%)
evidence.explanation: Quantifies how often the indication for this treatment arises. Directness is INDIRECT for the same broad-HCM reason.

treatments/9.description: Atrial fibrillation in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy carries a thromboembolic risk high enough that anticoagulation is recommended on the arrhythmia alone rather than gated on a general-population risk score. Roughly a fifth of patients develop atrial fibrillation and about a quarter of those experience thromboembolism.

treatments/9/targets/0.description: Anticoagulation does not treat the arrhythmia; it acts on the thromboembolic consequence that makes atrial fibrillation dangerous in this disease.

open_questions/0.rationale: This entry curates the SRX-destabilization arm as the mechanism of a large subset of MYH7 alleles rather than all of them, because not every cardiomyopathy myosin mutation shifts the SRX-DRX equilibrium. Two of the alleles with the best multiscale data illustrate the spread: G256E reduces the folded-back fraction by 33% through the transducer region, while R403Q has produced context-dependent and sometimes opposing measurements across assays. Without an allele-level map, a clinician cannot reason from a specific variant to the mechanism, and the SRX arm cannot be used to predict who will respond to a myosin inhibitor.

open_questions/1.rationale: Every clinical trial and outcome cohort cited in this entry enrolled hypertrophic cardiomyopathy broadly, not genotyped MYH7 carriers. That applies to both myosin inhibitors, to disopyramide, to beta-blockade and verapamil, to myectomy and alcohol septal ablation, to the ICD registry, to the anticoagulation review and to the LGE meta-analysis, and it is why no population prevalence exists for this entity. The gap is structural rather than incidental — genotype has not been a stratifying variable in HCM trial design — so it will not close through ordinary literature accumulation. Recorded so that a reader does not mistake the volume of clinical evidence here for evidence about MYH7.

evidence.snippet: Mice express the fast alpha-myosin in the heart, and orthologous ß-MyHC mutations do not lead to the phenotype typically found in HCM patients
evidence.explanation: States the isoform mismatch directly and asserts its translational consequence, which is what makes this a model-fidelity question rather than a general species caveat.

open_questions/2.rationale: The founding animal model of this disease carries R403Q in Myh6, not Myh7, because the adult mouse ventricle expresses alpha- rather than beta-myosin. Evidence therefore exists in the model but its translational validity is the open question, which is what distinguishes this from an ordinary knowledge gap. The pig study makes the mismatch explicit, stating that orthologous beta-MyHC mutations in mice do not produce the phenotype found in patients — and that is the stated reason large-animal models were built. Any claim in this entry that rests on mouse data inherits this caveat.

evidence.snippet: The p.L170* and E60Kfs5* variants are LOF, whereas p.W175* is hypomorphic when overexpressed.
evidence.explanation: The three new alleles and the functional class of each, including the one that establishes a partial form of the disease.

steps/1.description:
Eight variants are published across nine families. The 2023 five are all loss-of-expression or complete loss-of-function: two frameshift, one splice-site, and two in-frame 3-prime deletions both removing residues Ala133 to Lys181. The 2026 report adds p.Leu170* and p.Glu60Lysfs*5, both loss-of-function, and p.Trp175*, which is hypomorphic when overexpressed rather than null.
That last allele is the reason this entity now has a partial form. A nonsense variant at codon 175 of a 181-residue protein removes very little, and the patient who carries it was not BCG-vaccinated, stayed healthy through childhood, and presented at sixteen with weight loss and diarrhoea and at twenty-two with disseminated Mycobacterium abscessus. Allele severity and age at presentation move together.

evidence.snippet: Complete deficiency of this translation re-initiation factor impairs the translation of a subset of proteins, including the kinase JAK2 in all cell types tested, including T lymphocytes and phagocytes.
evidence.explanation: The molecular consequence and its scope — a subset of proteins, in every cell type looked at, which is what makes the narrowness of the clinical phenotype surprising.

evidence.snippet: Surprisingly, the lack of MCTS1-dependent translation re-initiation and ribosome recycling seems to be otherwise physiologically redundant in these patients.
evidence.explanation: The redundancy claim, quoted with the authors' own "seems to" intact. The 2026 series complicates it, which is why the hedge is preserved rather than paraphrased away.

steps/2.description:
MCTS1 heterodimerises with DENR to recycle 40S ribosomal subunits after termination and to permit reinitiation on messages carrying short upstream open reading frames. Without it, subunits are not released at stop codons and reinitiation downstream is impaired.
The striking part is how little this costs. The founding authors call MCTS1-dependent recycling "otherwise physiologically redundant" in these patients — meaning that outside the one pathway below, no phenotype attributable to a general translation defect was found. That is a strong claim and it is theirs, not this entry's; the 2026 series' growth failure, hypogammaglobulinaemia and gastrointestinal disease sit awkwardly against it, and this entry records both.

evidence.snippet: MCTS1 promotes JAK2 translation by reinitiating translation in the JAK2 5′UTR.
evidence.explanation: The mechanism stated compactly. Graded BACKGROUND because the 2026 paper is restating the 2023 finding in its introduction rather than reporting it, and HUMAN_CLINICAL because the work it summarises was done in patient and patient-derived cells.

steps/3.description:
This node is the specificity of the disease. The JAK2 5-prime untranslated region carries three upstream open reading frames, two of them ultra-short start-stop frames. Without MCTS1 to recycle them, 40S subunits stall at those stop codons and cannot reinitiate at the JAK2 main open reading frame.
It is why a general translation defect produces a single-pathway disease. Of seventeen genes of IFN-gamma immunity tested in MCTS1-knockout cells, only JAK2 showed a substantial translational decrease, rescued by wild-type MCTS1 and not by patient variants. A gene's vulnerability here is a property of its 5-prime untranslated region, not of its function.

evidence.snippet: JAK2 expression is sufficiently low to impair cellular responses to interleukin-23 (IL-23) and partially IL-12, but not other JAK2-dependent cytokines.
evidence.explanation: The quantitative threshold argument in the authors' own words — which cytokine responses the residual JAK2 supports and which it does not.

steps/4.description:
JAK2 falls in every cell type tested, including T lymphocytes and phagocytes. It does not fall to zero, and that quantitative detail is what makes the phenotype selective rather than global: the level is low enough to impair IL-23 responses and partially IL-12 responses, and not low enough to impair the other JAK2-dependent cytokine responses.
A JAK2 null would be a different and much worse disease — JAK2 carries erythropoietin, thrombopoietin and growth-hormone signalling. Nothing like that is seen here.

evidence.snippet: Defective responses to IL-23 preferentially impair the production of IFN-γ by innate-like adaptive mucosal-associated invariant T cells (MAIT) and γδ T lymphocytes upon mycobacterial challenge.
evidence.explanation: The step from cytokine signalling to effector function, naming the two lymphocyte populations that carry it.

steps/5.description:
IL-23 signalling is JAK2-dependent and is the response that fails here; IL-12 signalling is partially affected. The placement of this disease on the IL-23 limb rather than the IL-12 limb of the MSMD circuit is not an inference from the biochemistry — it was measured in patient cells, which showed impaired IL-23 responses with normal IL-12 responses.
That places IMD118 beside IL23R deficiency and IL-23 deficiency in the same functional pathway, and it is the reason the phenotype is mycobacterial rather than the broader susceptibility that IL-12 axis defects produce.

evidence.snippet: Adequate levels of JAK2 expression are required for IFN-γ production in response to IL-23 by innate-like adaptive T cells, such as Vδ2+ γδ T cells and mucosa-associated innate-like T cells
evidence.explanation: The pathway restated with the gamma-delta subset specified as Vdelta2-positive. Graded BACKGROUND because the 2026 paper is summarising its predecessor here.

steps/6.description:
MAIT cells and gamma-delta T cells produce less IFN-gamma on mycobacterial challenge. These are the lymphocytes that respond to mycobacteria without needing clonal expansion from a naive repertoire, which is why an infant meeting BCG in the first months of life depends on them.
Adequate JAK2 is required for exactly this, which is the 2026 authors' summary of the pathway and the reason the entity sits within MSMD rather than beside it.

evidence.snippet: Interferon-gamma (IFN-γ), a macrophage-activating factor (3), is at the heart of antimycobacterial immunity.
evidence.explanation: The general principle this node rests on, stated in the paper's introduction with its own citation. Graded BACKGROUND and INDIRECT because it is established immunology imported into this disease, not a measurement in an MCTS1 patient.

steps/7.description:
IFN-gamma is the macrophage-activating factor at the heart of antimycobacterial immunity, and without enough of it macrophages do not restrict the intracellular growth of weakly virulent mycobacteria. This is the step every MSMD genotype converges on, and it is established for the syndrome rather than measured in MCTS1 patients specifically.
Its most important property here is where it sits. The lesion is upstream of the IFN-gamma receptor and patient leukocytes respond normally to exogenous IFN-gamma, so this node can be driven from outside — which is what makes recombinant IFN-gamma a rational therapy rather than a hopeful one.

evidence.snippet: Three patients had adverse reactions to the BCG vaccine, whereas another patient was not vaccinated with BCG and had an infection with Mycobacterium abscessus at 16 years of age.
evidence.explanation: The split in the 2026 series between vaccinated and unvaccinated patients, which is the evidence that the vaccine is the usual trigger rather than the cause.

evidence.snippet: An empirical diagnosis of BCG-osis (affecting the brain, mastoid sinuses, lung, liver, and gastrointestinal tract) was established
evidence.explanation: The severe end of the range, in the patient who died — the organs involved when the disease is not controlled.

steps/8.description: The defining presentation. Eight of the nine published patients were BCG-vaccinated at or near birth and most developed disseminated BCG disease between one and twelve months. The 2026 series shows the range: axillary adenitis with bone-marrow involvement at four months, abscessed BCG adenitis at seven months, local armpit disease at one month, and in one patient a BCG-osis involving brain, mastoid sinuses, lung, liver and gastrointestinal tract that was fatal.

evidence.snippet: The patient was diagnosed with disseminated M. abscessus infection manifesting as bulky intra-abdominal/retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy, chronic diarrhea, and chronic weight loss.
evidence.explanation: The full presentation in the unvaccinated adult patient.

steps/9.description: Disseminated Mycobacterium abscessus in the unvaccinated American patient, presenting as bulky intra-abdominal and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy with chronic diarrhoea and weight loss, and Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex on ileocaecal mucosal biopsy in the Chinese patient. Environmental mycobacteria are what these patients meet when BCG is not given.

evidence.snippet: At the age of 4 mo, he presented BCG-osis with left axillary adenitis.
evidence.explanation: The regional adenitis in the youngest of the 2026 patients, with its age.

steps/10.description: Regional adenitis at the vaccination site in the BCG patients, and bulky intra-abdominal and retroperitoneal conglomerate lymphadenopathy in the adult with M. abscessus — in his case a retroperitoneal mass encasing the aorta and the proximal coeliac and superior mesenteric arteries, with necrotic change.

evidence.snippet: Immunological analyses revealed that P1 had low immunoglobulin (IG) levels, despite having normal total serum protein and albumin levels. Intravenous IG (IVIG) treatment was therefore initiated.
evidence.explanation: The finding with the controls that make it a genuine hypogammaglobulinaemia rather than a dilutional or loss-related artefact.

evidence.snippet: He also receives IFN-γ-1b and IVIG due to his hypogammaglobulinemia (Tables S3 and S4).
evidence.explanation: The second instance, in the Chinese patient, alongside his IFN-gamma treatment.

steps/11.description:
Low immunoglobulins with normal total protein and albumin in the youngest 2026 patient, treated with intravenous immunoglobulin; hypogammaglobulinaemia in the Chinese patient, also on replacement; moderately low B cell counts and IgG in the Omani patient.
This is the finding that sits least comfortably with the founding description of an otherwise intact immune system. Three of the four 2026 patients received immunoglobulin replacement.

evidence.snippet: At 3.5 years old, his weight was 10.5 kg, and he was 77 cm tall (both these growth parameters are below the third percentile).
evidence.explanation: The measured growth failure, with the centile, in the youngest 2026 patient.

steps/12.description: Weight and height below the third percentile at three and a half years in the youngest 2026 patient; failure to thrive with height and weight below the third percentile and delayed gross motor development in the Omani patient. Chronic weight loss in the adult with M. abscessus.

evidence.snippet: A mucosal biopsy specimen from this area tested positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex by metagenomic next-generation sequencing.
evidence.explanation: That the gastrointestinal disease is mycobacterial, established on tissue rather than inferred from the systemic diagnosis.

steps/13.description:
Recurrent diarrhoea from age six in the Chinese patient, leading at ten to colonoscopy that found an ileocaecal ulcer positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex; chronic diarrhoea with abdominal distension, ascites and pancolitis in the Omani patient; chronic diarrhoea in the American patient with M. abscessus.
The gut is a mycobacterial site in this disease, not merely a site of nonspecific symptoms — which matters because a chronic diarrhoea in a patient already on antimycobacterial therapy invites a search for a different cause.

evidence.snippet: The local infection gradually improved, but P3 has suffered from recurrent diarrhea since the age of 6 years and recurrent otitis media since the age of 9 years.
evidence.explanation: The two chronic problems that followed the resolved BCG disease in this patient.

steps/14.description: Recurrent otitis media from age nine in the Chinese patient, and otomastoiditis on imaging in the Omani patient during his fatal illness.

evidence.snippet: Cranial computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging revealed otomastoiditis, acute cerebral venous thrombosis, and granulomatous meningitis with focal white matter lesions that were particularly abundant in the right hemisphere.
evidence.explanation: The imaging findings that established central nervous system involvement.

evidence.snippet: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) culture revealed the presence of pyrazinamide-resistant M. bovis–BCG.
evidence.explanation: The organism, cultured from cerebrospinal fluid, with its resistance pattern — which is what makes this BCG disease of the central nervous system rather than a sterile inflammatory process.

steps/15.description: Central nervous system BCG disease in the Omani patient: generalised tonic-clonic seizure at six, imaging showing otomastoiditis, acute cerebral venous thrombosis and granulomatous meningitis with focal white-matter lesions, pyrazinamide-resistant M. bovis BCG cultured from cerebrospinal fluid, then breakthrough seizures, status epilepticus and new lesions. He died at six years and nine months.

edges/9.description: Regional then disseminated nodal disease is how BCG spreads from the vaccination site.

edges/10.description: Central nervous system involvement in the patient in whom BCG disease was not controlled, with the organism cultured from cerebrospinal fluid.

edges/11.description: Chronic mycobacterial infection is itself a cause of growth failure. Whether it is the only cause here is the question recorded in this entry's redundancy discussion.

edges/12.description: The gastrointestinal tract is one of the organs BCG disseminates to, and in one patient the ileocaecal lesion was mycobacterium-positive on biopsy.

edges/13.description: Bulky intra-abdominal and retroperitoneal nodal disease is the presenting manifestation of the M. abscessus infection in the unvaccinated adult patient.

edges/14.description: Chronic diarrhoea accompanied the disseminated abdominal disease in that patient and the ileocaecal tuberculous ulcer in another.

edges/15.description: Recurrent bacterial otitis is the expected consequence of an antibody deficit rather than of the IFN-gamma induction defect, which is why it is drawn from here rather than from the mycobacterial chain.

evidence.snippet: These findings suggest that X-linked recessive human MCTS1 deficiency underlies isolated mycobacterial disease by impairing JAK2 translation in innate-like adaptive T lymphocytes, thereby impairing the IL-23-dependent induction of IFN-γ.
evidence.explanation: The gene-disease claim and the mechanism in one sentence, as the authors state it.

genes/0.notes:
The single causal gene.
